And I would like you to focus on, please, a very minor point. On 5.5. So it would be paragraph 5 -- I'm sorry. I mean 5.6, 5.6. This is the order prepared with respect to the attack on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read 5.6, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it basically states that his reserve during that operation will be the military police; is that correct, the military police platoon? That's their function, as reserve.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order issued by the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade, dated the 5th of July, and this is what it says in 5.6: That reserve military police platoon have it in the area of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade command post, ready to deploy if need be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here's how you can help, all this controversy that we had last week. Because Lieutenant-- I mean, Captain, not even First Class Nikolic --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the lead-in, statements, that's improper. He's supposed to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: According to Captain Nikolic, and I'm reading from the transcript, and it's on page 1950, dated 25 September 2003, and I'll have to read just a portion of it, line 13. It says: "With an order of this kind, with an assignment to the military police of this kind, violations have been made first of the authorities of the brigade commander and his competencies and the military police unit was engaged in matters that did not come under the realm of military police assignments." That's Nikolic's opinion with respect to using the military police as reserve, and also he states later on that -- and if I can find it here in a second. One second here. I'll move on. Let me ask you this, Mr. Obrenovic: You used your military police on a combat operation. Here Colonel Blagojevic is using his military police to be in a reserve during a combat operation. Do you see anything improper with the use of the military police in this fashion, the way that Captain Nikolic has described?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I really don't know what Captain Nikolic said here, but according to certain rules about the military police from the JNA, which we used there, the truth is that the basic purpose of the military police is not to participate in combat. The military police is intended for other purposes, to secure command posts, commanders, and it has other tasks, so we won't waste time going into all those. But it is also true that situations were often -- well, I won't say unforeseeable, but very often things that hadn't been planned, happened. And circumstances often required that we use units, including the military police, for purposes other than those for which they had been intended. So the military police were sometimes used not only to perform military police tasks but also to engage in combat. As you have seen, I used that squad for reconnaissance, which you just mentioned. And perhaps Captain Nikolic was right, because the military police is not a reconnaissance squad; I should have used reconnaissance men, but I didn't have any. So that's why I used the military police. As I said, I haven't read what Nikolic said here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And have you familiarised yourself with the rules for the military police as far as what they can and cannot be engaged in, especially during times of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes. It's a long time since I read the combat rules about the use of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did your intelligence officer or security officer, Drago Nikolic, raise any objections with the way you were using your military police for actual combat as opposed to keeping them in reserve, or as the reserve?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, he asked that a military police company be put at his disposal, and I told him they were already in the field, that we didn't have another company at our disposal. He then insisted that at least Captain Jasikovac, with one platoon, be put at his disposal, and I said I'd see what I could do and I let Jasikovac and five or six soldiers go. I can't be precise about the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I guess my question is: Before engaging them, before the 13th, when you actually engaged them, did he raise any objections with you to say, "you know, Mr. Acting Commander, what are you doing, you know, using the military police for these purposes? You're improperly using them." Did he raise any objections?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day, that is, the 12th, when I sent the first group up there, I told him in the corridor, I said, "Drago, we have no other units, so we have to send some of the military police in Zaselje," before he asked me anything, because I was aware of the fact that he could ask something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it was your decision to send them up there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As it was your decision to bring them back and then task them with the tasks that you gave them on the night of the 13th and then 14th, and so on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told Captain Jasikovac that he should stay there and that he should report to Drago Nikolic or that he would be called by him, and that he would receive his orders from him. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say - and I don't want to dwell on this issue - but would it be fair to say that by bringing back the part of the military police and actually tasking them, you were in essence individually involving yourself into this operation to kill the prisoners, as opposed to just merely as a superior, commander, now you were individually involving yourself? Would that be a fair way to characterise your involvement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to switch to another topic, and if we could talk about this term that has been used quite often. There I go again. I'm making -- I'm stating something. If we could talk about what is commonly referred to in this courtroom as "zone of responsibility," that whole concept, okay? All right. Obviously, you've heard the term before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, I believe I've come across some of your -- some things in writing by you, maybe even orally, where you've even used the term "zone of responsibility." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, does the brigade, a brigade, not a corps, but does a brigade have a zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, for me to give a precise answer, we would have to look at the rules and regulations for infantry motorised and mountain brigades of the JNA, those rules and regulations, because they refer to several concepts: First of all, the zone of intelligence responsibility, the zone of defence -- I don't know if I've forgotten any of them. The zone of responsibility is - how shall I put this - a derived term, and you won't find it in the rules if you stick to the rules and regulations. You won't find it stipulated there, in addition to the other rules and instructions for the work of commands and headquarters in the JNA. But it is a concept that was used there. And you quite rightly stated that in some documents from the corps command, from that period of time, you might also find it used there. And if I remember correctly, the corps command at one point in time designated the points, and perhaps I showed this on the map the other day. I think I did. And in that order it referred to the zone of responsibility, which I pointed out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, before we get to the rules - and I do have them here, and we can go through them. There are only three on each side - does the corps, the Drina Corps, have a zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that zone of responsibility is quite different than any zones, or a zone of responsibility - and I hate using that term for the brigades - but it's quite different than what is tasked to the brigades?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. The corps command is an operative command. Brigades are associated commands or lower levels of commands and you're quite right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you help us out here a little bit. You're a military expert. Could you tell us a little bit about what does a zone of responsibility for the corps encompass? And if it would be helpful, we can use one of the Prosecutor's maps, one of their charts, and maybe you can help us out there. That might assist us. But I'll leave it up to you. Maybe you want to give us the description and then we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could I cut in, if you don't mind? Mr. McCloskey, have you ever introduced a map indicating the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps, Bratunac Brigade or the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I believe there's a map in the indictment that has the -- if we're talking about geographic borders, which I'm not exactly sure if they're talking about that or not yet. But we -- the indictment has the rough -- you know, it's a rough map of geographic borders. This map -- the military map behind me also has the northern border of the Drina Corps, as the witness pointed out, and it also has the front lines. It doesn't go all the way down. Ms. Stewart has reminded me: We have P85, which went in through Mr. Nikolic, and Mr. Butler will talk about it, and it does have the geographic borders written on it, based on many things that Mr. Butler has studied. So that's just a rough recollection of this geographic zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It's very helpful. Maybe we could use this map, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for the assistance, Your Honour, and I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we could put that map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you could just take a look at the map and just get your bearings. And I guess -- I just want some general questions to be answered. If you could just show us with the pointer, and for identification purposes, this is what again? P -- I just want -- P85. Okay. I just want to make my record. If you could demonstrate on what has been marked as P85 where the zone of the Drina Corps is, in a geographical sense, what it encompasses, so we can visualise it.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, on this document numbered P85, if I can see this correctly, all it provides is the northern part of the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps. So what is lacking here is the southern portion, which encompasses geographic entities, the built-up areas, inhabited areas, from Han Pijesak onwards, which means Sokolac, Rogatica, Visegrad, parts of the Gorazde municipality, and, if I remember correctly, the territory of part of the municipality of Cajnice. So that part is lacking on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, maybe during the break the Prosecution can furnish us with a better map or a larger map. I don't know. But we'll try to deal with that technical issue. But would it be fair to say that when we're talking about a zone of responsibility for the corps, a corps, on the map you could actually draw a border, and everything within this border would be part of the zone of responsibility of a corps? Am I correct or am I oversimplifying it or am I just off?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And within this sort of geographical, if we could sort of visualise a pie, you know, within this, some sections are designated within this pie to the various brigades?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And those areas that are not given to any particular brigade still remain part of the zone of responsibility of the corps. So the corps is responsible, in other words, for those sections of the pie that are not taken up by the various brigades. It's a crude analogy, but I think it might help us out here.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the explanation and interpretation of the military rules and regulations, the corps is still responsible, regardless of whether it's the lower command that is responsible. So for the zone of the brigade, this does not make the responsibility of the corps any less, just as the command of the brigade is responsible for what goes on in the battalion area, following on from the same logics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But I guess what I'm trying to suggest, and correct me in I'm misstating the case, that within this geographic region, this zone of responsibility of the corps, there are sections that are not designated to any particular brigade. You don't know?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's take, for instance, Zvornik. Was the Zvornik Brigade responsible for the municipality of Zvornik? You were there. You were called Zvornik Brigade. Your headquarters were in Zvornik. Was the municipality part of the zone of responsibility, or whatever we want to call it - we're going to get more technical later - of the Zvornik Brigade, or was it part of the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, what we had was an order from the command of the Drina Corps stipulating several points, perhaps six or seven. I can enumerate them later on. But the zone was precisely defined, that zone of responsibility. As I said, the rules provided for things in a different way. And if I recall, you won't find the zone of responsibility mentioned in the rules and regulations. But also if my memory serves me, there was an order by the corps commander, for instance, probably dated 1994, whatever the year was, which - I don't know for what reason exactly - did define quite precisely those zones of responsibility. So that's how they existed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me try another way. I want to refer to your statement. You gave a statement to the Prosecution on 4 June 2003. Do you remember giving a statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And during the statement -- let me see if I can find the right page. It's only a small ... You were asked a series of questions, and now I'm going to read a section. It's from page 8, and it's lines 16 to 20. And you're being asked by Peter McCloskey, the gentleman there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, sorry. That was a two-part question. And you were the person that was in charge that evening in Zvornik. That was the question, "in Zvornik." Your answer:

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the Zvornik Brigade, not for Zvornik. Now, from here, it seems to -- you seem to be implying that you weren't responsible for Zvornik, meaning the municipality of Zvornik, but you were in charge of Zvornik Brigade. Do I have it wrong?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You read it out correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And you, as the brigade -- well, you were sitting in as the deputy commander at the time, but even when Pandurevic was there, he was not responsible for the municipality. That wasn't his zone of responsibility, the municipality itself.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that the order from the corps commander was received exactly by the Zvornik Brigade. Let me take it from the north. Along the Drina River, a feature 141. It's not here, but I know it by heart. Then there's a road, a path, called Konjski Put, and the hill there. Then there's the Praznitorba facility, once again not on the map. And then we went round in order, the Spreca River, then further on from the river to Kozluk, from Kozluk to Udrc, to Kuslat, to Milovan, and once again to the Drina River, with those features. And somewhere in the documents we can find an exact description of this zone of defence. I said that -- in response to Mr. McCloskey that I wasn't the chief in Zvornik. The Zvornik municipality is a complex community. You'll find factories, hospitals there, and what have you, millions of other things. So as the deputy commander, I was responsible for the units which were located there, and that's what I meant when I said that. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who controls the area between one brigade and the other, if there is a gap? Who controls that? A particular brigade or is it part of the corps' responsibility to provide the protection?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to be precise in responding to your question, our left neighbour was the 1st Birac Brigade and the border went along the Spreca River to the facilities I mentioned a moment ago, towards Udrc and there was no gap. You knew that it was the Zvornik Brigade, pukovnik Andric, under whose responsibility that was. And towards Colonel Blagojevic's brigade, the border ran or the zone of responsibility ran from the Drina River, that is to say the southern side -- border of the municipality of Zvornik, up to Milovan, which was a feature there, and Kuslat. That was their zone. So our brigade had no gap. Now, how this was resolved in other areas, I can't say. I assume that the corps commander ordered something. But I can't be more specific than what I've just told you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand -- well, let's go through the rules. If I can show you what has been premarked for identification purposes as P83. These are the brigade rules. And also D51. D51 and P83. And for the record, D51 are the rule corps [sic] of ground forces. Now, this is dated 1990, so it's post-events. But if you could look at it, and maybe if they were still relevant or applicable at the time, we could discuss it. And also the brigade rules dated 1984. And you may wish to look at, on D51 - we'll take it step by step - rule 5. So you may wish to look at also rule 3 and 4, but primarily rule 5. And its counterpart in P83, the brigade rules, rule 13.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And have you had a chance to look both at the rule 5 of the corps and rule 13 of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. Just for clarity --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe he's referring to paragraph numbers. This is -- this whole document is a rule, but just for clarity, I think this is paragraph number. It's not a rule number or an article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We'll look at paragraph number 5 under the corps and paragraph 13 under the brigade rules. Have you had a chance to look at both?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in reading these two paragraphs, corresponding paragraphs, is there a difference between what is allocated or given to a corps versus what the corps allocates to the brigade, as far as a geographic allocation of territory? I don't know if that -- if you can understand my question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. As it says here in the two paragraphs mentioned, there is a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And at least with respect to the brigade rules, or the brigade -- paragraph number 13, with respect to the zone -- we have a zone of operation; right? And not a zone of responsibility; right? It says "zone of operation." Is that correct? I'm doing it step by step, so we don't draw any objections.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And a moment ago, that's what I told you when you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know, but ... And then in which to carry out its tasks. And then you have a zone of attack, the zone of defence, the zone of march, and suchlike. That's what's stated in those rules, right, in paragraph 13 of the brigade rule? Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, the zone of operation for the brigade is a ground space of limited width and depth, in which a brigade organises and carries out combat operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, who designates that ground space of limited, limited width and depth? Who designates that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps command does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on what basis is that designated? I mean, what are the criteria? I mean, if you know. That they would look at and say: Okay. To the Bratunac Brigade, given the fact that they only have so many soldiers and we need to cover this amount of territory, given that they have this neighbour and that neighbour, with these sorts of resources. What are the criteria?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as you probably know, I never worked in the corps command. But perhaps I can use the experience gained from the brigade command when designating regions for the battalion's defence, the brigade command would then have in mind first of all the composition and combat capabilities of the unit concerned, that is the battalion, and secondly, the geographical characteristics of the terrain on which combat operations are to take place; and third, the expected predicted enemy forces in the ground space concerned, the communications, roads, obstacles, and similar features. Perhaps the corps command would think along those lines. It's an operative command. I never worked there and I don't have any experience in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think that covers it, and I think you might also throw in the mission, because you've indicated number of soldiers, equipment, the terrain, the enemy disposition and capability, and I take it also the mission.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the combat assignment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, how did the depth of the Zvornik Brigade, did that also encompass the entire municipality of Zvornik, the town itself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, an answer to your question would require complexity. To all intents and purposes, throughout the war, there was a certain - I don't know if I'm going to use the right term here - parallelism, between what was set according to the rules and what daily life required. Let me put this in another way. The zone of responsibility of a motorised brigade would have had to be a broad section of the front, that is to say, underneath -- below 15 kilometres. In a mountainous terrain that would be 12 to 15 kilometres. I might be out one or two kilometres. And in depth, this would be the same for the rear. Now, as you can see on this map here, and as you can see with the naked eye, this zone of defence, the front, was 45 kilometres long, which means two or three times, three times the amount provided for by the rules and regulations. Because the defence was organised in linear form, without the deployment of the battalion in depth. So what we tried to do was --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Slow down a little bit, just a little bit. Slow down. Wonderful answer, but slow down a little bit, for the ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Yes. What I was going to say is this: The rules were one thing, and the commands tried within the frameworks of their possibilities and feasibility to put them into practice. And then I quoted this other example of the defence front of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So given the amount of manpower that you had available, you had a particular terrain that you needed to cover, a line, and then you had a certain amount of territory looking forward and territory depth backwards, and that was your zone of operation. Am I correct in stating that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And behind that area, if it was within, within the corps zone of responsibility, I take it that the corps would be responsible for that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Vague. It's impossible to tell what area he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe, Mr. Karnavas, you did not put yourself very clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you are tired, and it's time for a break. Shall we break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I hope the fatigue is not showing, but we could use the break, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But I have to remind you that I hope you could finish your cross-examination before 1.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll be frank. I'll be frank. You're giving me a Herculean task and I'm certainly not of any calibre of Hercules to finish that in that amount of time. At the end of the day I can assure you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Try your best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying, I'm trying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Try your best. During the break I hope you could somehow streamline your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do also want to note that these are critical issues. I know they don't seem at this point, but we do have a military expert. It's a Prosecution expert. But these are -- I'm laying the groundwork for what is to come and I certainly don't want to bring Mr. Obrenovic back as my witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And another thing that we could ask the Prosecution to do us a favour. I wonder whether you could furnish us with a map indicating the zone of responsibility of the various units, as well as the zone of the Srebrenica safe area, the area which controlled by the BiH army, so that we can have a clear picture of how things -- it's just geographic, you know, indications, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this military map behind me I believe is the -- it was done by the Zvornik Brigade. I think it's very reliable. The northern border of the Zvornik Brigade and the Drina River and the front line. It doesn't go as far down as Rogatica, so we don't have the whole Drina Corps, but I don't see how that's really relevant. We can try to find a map of the southern border. I don't think we have one. But it is in a rough map of the indictment. This exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm interested in the border areas between the two brigades, which is relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, the exhibit, P85, as you know, is not the precise geographic map as the other one, but it has the rough drawing of what Mr. Butler's study has revealed regarding those brigades. The best way to determine that, and I hate to put the witness to any work, but he knows them precisely. He can describe them. And I'm sure, if given the chance, he can mark, from his knowledge, those markings. We have them. I believe they're roughly correct in this simple map, and they're marked in -- I believe in green. If the witness could be asked about that. But the precise areas would be best drawn on that map. We did not find a map that had all of these on them. It's a compilation of our knowledge. That is a reflection of the compilation of our knowledge, that map right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it would be much helpful if we have that map or the future witness, not only for this one, so would you please try your best, while incorporating the testimony of this witness, to furnish us with a map indicating the zone of responsibility, at a later stage, not now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This map has it, Your Honour. If I could explain it to you, I could show it to you. And if you would like it in a more detailed, a topographic map, we can do that also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe at a later stage. Yes. We'll resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Obrenovic, we were speaking about zones before we took our break. Before we get to the map: Were you -- was your zone -- did your zone also encompass the Zvornik town?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In practical terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you were in charge of the traffic police over there? You understand English, so please: Were you in charge of the traffic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. This is argumentative, and it's a suggestion that he's avoiding the question, which is, after all the hard work this witness has done -- not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I object to the speechmaking about the hard work of the witness. He's a witness like any other, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's a small matter. It is not worth that kind of argument. Just ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there a competent civil authority for the Zvornik town; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were they not in charge of the town, or was it the colonel -- Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, and in his absence Major Obrenovic, in town of the Zvornik town and the Zvornik municipality? Who was in charge?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the town, as a built-up area, I think it's unnecessary to explain. This is a built-up area where civilians live, where life goes on, quite apart from military elements. Who was in charge there? It was, conditionally speaking, the civilian authorities. Perhaps they did not exist, but there were certain institutions of civilian organisation. I won't go into that in detail, but there were two parallel systems there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You say conditionally speaking. Are you suggesting that there was -- well, the civilian authority was in charge of the Zvornik town and the municipality; isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And it wasn't that the Zvornik Brigade was in charge of the town, then; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the town. Not for the elements that were independent of the army. Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, they had their own police force, for instance. In other words, you didn't engage your military police to be patrolling the streets, to be engaged in traffic control in Zvornik town; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, the military police of the Zvornik Brigade was tasked with military police assignments, regulating the military traffic in the area of Zvornik, checking the identity of soldiers wherever they may be. The military police performed tasks falling within its competence, regardless of whether this was in Zvornik or Karakaj or any other place. Of course they had nothing to do with the civilian population or with civilian traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So they were not -- that's my whole point. They were not engaged in the functions of the civilian functions for Zvornik with respect to policing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And would that, by analogy, also apply, say, in Bratunac? Would the Bratunac Brigade, for instance, also be in charge of Bratunac town?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Vague and overbroad question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you understand the question, Mr. Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, at that time I was not in Bratunac, but by analogy, one might suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, under the rules, the corps, does it not have -- the corps. I'm not talking about the brigade. Does the corps not have a geographic border where that's -- their zone of responsibility is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And does that not encompass, within their geographic border, does it not encompass towns, such as Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It encompasses everything within the zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Including the areas where the particular brigades are not taking up. Because as you've indicated, you have a particular line with a certain depth and a certain amount of forward territory that you're responsible for; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a little while ago that as for the zones of brigades, I can speak about the Zvornik Brigade and our left-hand neighbours, the 1st Birac Brigade, and the Bratunac Brigade, which was our neighbour in depth. As for the others, I really couldn't reply with any precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, if we looked at the particular zones -- let me put it this way. If we looked at the particular areas that each brigade covered within the Drina Corps zone of responsibility, would that cover the entire geographical area? If you don't know the answer, just say: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the part I mentioned, it did. But as for the other parts, I don't know. The concept of zone of responsibility, which does not exist in the rules of an infantry brigade, was used in 1994, or perhaps earlier, by the corps command, in an order that they issued. I remember that we in Zvornik commented upon this, that this was not according to the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, perhaps you can assist us here a little bit. I want to focus you on your statement of 4 June 2003. I believe it's -- I'm going to read from pages 62, starting with line 27, all the way to page 63, line 6. And I'll ask you if you recall making this statement, and then we'll discuss it. On page -- on line 25, Peter McCloskey is asking you the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Oppose what? And then you answer:

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladic's idea that these people should be shot. I think he said that Mladic was surrounded by a group of people who were sycophants and afraid to stand up to him, and that was not good. You're referring to Pandurevic. This is the conversation you're having with Pandurevic. "I asked him: 'Should we do something about it? Because it was our defence zone.'" Defence zone. "He said: 'What is there for us to do? It is well known who ordered it, who carried it out. And this is all in the zone of the main headquarters.' And as far as anything in writing is concerned, according to him," meaning Pandurevic, "those reports are sufficient. Furthermore he mentioned and he was angry that the commander of civil defence in Zvornik, who refused to take part in the burials when he requested," meaning he, Pandurevic," and then he declined, a quarrel ensued between them and he said he would subsequently settle that with him." Do you recall having this conversation with Mr. McCloskey? This happened to be one of the tape-recorded ones. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, and that's what I said. It's possible that it may have been misinterpreted to me. I think I said Main Staff, not main command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so when you're talking about the Main Staff and their zone, you're talking, in essence, the entire RS territory; right? It stands to reason.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then within that territory, you have one geographical region given to one corps, such as the Drina Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then, as we said, within that geographical region, you have these zones of defence of the particular brigades, which are based on tasks as opposed to a geographic territory. Am I correct in stating it in those terms?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Is there any part that you wish to clarify? Because I'm not trying to -- I don't want to put words in your mouth and I'm not trying to misrepresent the facts or what is under the rules.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a short explanation is necessary in relation to -- let's use the expression "invented term zone of responsibility of a brigade. As I said, this term was invented, or rather, used by the command of the Drina Corps in some of the orders they issued. I think it may have been in 1994. So in any case, it was considerably before these events. And for reasons known to them, they divided up part of the territory, and I'm referring to the part that relates to the north part of their zone of responsibility, where they made a precise list of the zone of responsibility of the brigades, that is, the Zvornik Brigade, to be precise. And you are quite right; this concept does not exist under the rules and regulations. Why they did this, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, focusing back to this little conversation that you had between -- with your commander, I want to focus on his response with respect to the civil authorities, the civil defence in Zvornik. Now, when we're talking about the civil defence, we're talking of a civil versus a military authority, are we not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, perhaps this is being misinterpreted to me. I said civilian protection, not civil defence. I don't know English very well, but in the Serbian language, these two concepts are quite distinct. And if I recall well, I talked to Mr. McCloskey of civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I apologise if I'm confusing you on top of that, so let me make sure I have it right. The civil protection, at least from the sounds of it, seems to me like we're talking about a civilian authority versus the military authority. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's a civilian institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, can we conclude from Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic's little remark to you, can we conclude -- or is he implying that the municipalities, or the Zvornik at the time, was not under military control, and therefore, that's why he was unable to exercise any of his own authority to get the civil defence to do what he wanted them to do?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I object to the form of the question. It says: Can we conclude or can we imply. The question says yes, we don't know if he's made a conclusion or an implication and I know this will be used in argument down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well taken, Your Honour. I see the errors of my ways. I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: In other words, that is the military control is not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Military control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. It's not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, thank you, Your Honour. Thank you for pointing that out. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, let me just -- let me go about it in another way. From what Mr. Pandurevic is saying, does he not seem to be implying that the municipalities were not under military control? And we'll get to the control part. That he had no control over the civil defence, the civil authority?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I understood you correctly. When you said "municipality," we are referring to the geographic concept or to a body of -- a local government body?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A local government body.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local political authority was not under military command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, they were independent, were they not? They were autonomous?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In relation to Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, yes, if that's your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, in relation to the military, the Zvornik Brigade, the administrative authorities, the civilian administrative authorities in Zvornik, were autonomous from, say, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this is a good example where -- at least Mr. Pandurevic seems to be indicating that he could not get the civil defence to comply with a particular order or request that he had made or that had been made to him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he means civil protection again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Civil protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Remember Tito. This is a big difference in this world.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, I think we can move on. I think we can move on. I want to talk a little bit about the security organ right now. And there was an instruction that was shown to you yesterday, and as I believe, it was identified as D22/1 for identification purposes. If I could show that to you again, we can briefly discuss that. Did you have an opportunity to read it thoroughly yesterday, when you looked at it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I skimmed through it, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Might I conclude from your -- from this answer that you did not go over this in depth, either with your lawyers or with Mr. McCloskey, prior to coming here today? Looking at it is one thing, but actually going into it concretely in depth.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I think that Mr. McCloskey and I looked at it, and I looked at it with my lawyers in -- well, more seriously, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were you aware of this particular policy, the policy that set in -- maybe not the document, but the policy that's set into this particular document that's been identified as D22, were you aware of it back then, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Foundation. What policy? I think he first needs to identify if there is a policy before he can ask such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, yesterday you discussed this under direct examination when Mr. McCloskey was asking you questions. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, yes. You heard that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And having read this, does this document not set out or give instructions with respect to the security organ within the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. These are listed in several paragraphs. Eight certain things are listed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this particular instruction was handed down by General Mladic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't be precise about that, Mr. Karnavas, but all I can say is that the heading of this document bears the title "Headquarters of Republika Srpska Army," and that Commander Ratko Mladic's name is typed here, but somebody else signed for him. I don't know who. That's the best answer I can give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And brief -- well, let me ask you this: Do you know whether any rules existed prior to the issuance of this instruction that detailed how the security organ was supposed to function within the VRS?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. At that time, as we've already mentioned, wherever the VRS did not have its own rules, the rules of the JNA were applied. It was common knowledge that there was a rule on the work of the security organs in the JNA - I don't know from what year - and there was also a rule on the military police, and an instruction on the implementation of the rule on military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, does this document set out any policy directives or instructions on how the commanders are to relate to the security organs within their commands?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. Policy directives and instructions can be two entirely different things, and we're in the multi-part question problem again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll rephrase --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In this instruction, does General Mladic set out certain policies? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I wouldn't call it a policy. An instruction in the military rules is a very precise concept. It's issued by the Main Staff, and I don't know it by heart, but you can find the definition in the rules. The Main Staff, or Mladic, as you said, through this instruction, gives certain practical tasks in relation to command, security organs -- or rather, security organs in commands that have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, if there were rules, why was it necessary for Mladic to also issue instructions. Why doesn't Mladic send a letter saying: From now on, everybody should apply the rules that we have? Why is it necessary for him to produce this rather detailed instruction?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, this question is not that relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Looking at paragraph number 2, at the bottom of the paragraph. It says: "Besides, all members of such agencies and services, have lawful authority to proceed on tasks within their scope of work, and those correspond to the authorities of members of the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs state security department." What do you understand that to mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. What paragraph did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Paragraph number 2, the last sentence.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The commander of units may be consulted about these issues," is that it? I apologise. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Paragraph number -- there are paragraphs that are numbered, at least the English version.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if you go to number 2, there's a number of it, and I'm referring to a section that the last -- the last sentence in that paragraph, paragraph number 2, where it talks about internal affairs and state security department. Did you read that? Does this not seem to imply that now the security organ is becoming more like an institution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, Mr. Karnavas, that this sets out some rights given to the security organs, in actual fact, and they are given those rights which, according to the law, are rights enjoyed by members of the MUP and the state security sector. Now, I can speculate as to what this refers to, but I'm sure that the laws -- that the law sets out which rights the organs have. Perhaps to ask people taken into custody to show their ID cards or to take people into custody, in fact, or things of that kind. Now, whether it's an institution or not an institution, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The RS -- well, would you say that the RS Ministry of Internal Affairs, is that a particular organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand this correctly, the Ministry of Internal Affairs is an organ of the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And what --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then you have the state security department, which is within the Ministry of the Interior -- of Internal Affairs; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the set-up of the organisation in those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Let's go to paragraph number 3. And I'll just -- we'll read along together: "It is an obligation of all RS units and institution commands, as well as the obligation of other army members, to render any assistance to these agencies required to accomplish their tasks without jeopardising, through a single act, the security and protection of planned intelligence or counter-intelligence tasks and actions undertaken locally as well as in an enemy territory."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I know it was just a slip of the tongue, but it was meant to be VRS units, not RS units. There's actually a major difference, and Mr. Karnavas, I've got the recent translation, if you want to use that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The VRS. We'll use VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, it says here -- it seems to be setting out a policy or an obligation, okay, as to what the VRS units and institutions of commands vis-a-vis, in relation to, the security organs; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In other words, you don't have a choice. You are obliged. It's a requirement.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says it is a requirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's look at the next sentence: "Simultaneously," at the same time, that is, "simultaneously, it is a duty of the members of the security intelligence agencies to directly inform their superior commanders to a necessary extent," and I'm underscoring that part, I'm highlighting that part, to a necessary extent," on the data, assessment, and observations related to security of units-institutions." Did you find that part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Is there anything wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a completely different translation from the official translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm unaware that his version is the official translation. I can read the other translation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It might make it easier for the interpreters, who usually should have the official interpretation. The CLSS interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, would you please offer your version of this translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. And we, of course, as you recall, back when we did this, and I will give up mine. If we could get it on the ELMO so I could see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's focus on the first part. It says: "At the same time, simultaneously, to the extent and in the measure necessary," as is necessary, okay. Now, let's stop right there. Does this not seem to mean that they have some discretion, that is, the security organ exercises its discretion, based on how that is phrased, that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to their assessment, or the assessment of the security organ of the Superior Command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicated that at one point you had a first lieutenant, not even a captain, in the Zvornik Brigade who apparently was giving your commander, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, let's say some grief over how he, that is, the first lieutenant, should be conducting his tasks as the chief of the security organ. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said something similar to Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And in fact, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic tried to control him, in a sense of trying to control his actions, but was more or less overruled by higher authorities, particularly because this first lieutenant was a member of the -- was the chief of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. Vagueness. This needs specificity to be proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think the question has got a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was the question vague for you, sir, or are you capable of answering it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's not proper to ask this kind of question to the witness himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At some point, Your Honour, the objections are designed to disrupt and obstruct, and at some point a question such as this is like a shot over the bow of the Prosecution. Because we're trying to get to somewhere with this particular gentleman, and this information was elicited on direct and I'm trying to go deeper into the subject matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Then you can do it step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Lay your foundations first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You indicated there were some problems between your command, Pandurevic, colonel, with this first lieutenant, Drago Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I said that certain problems arose in the winter of 1994, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And why did those problems come up? What was the problem? What caused this discontent?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not to speak in general terms, at one point Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic was not satisfied with the method of work of Lieutenant Colonel Drago Nikolic, and he ordered him, in future -- he said that Nikolic couldn't use the brigade stamp in future to accompany his signature, that no documents should go out from the brigade command encrypted without the commander's signature, and some similar things. If you want, I can go through them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was trying to control Nikolic, as I indicated earlier, control his actions and his behaviour.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, in a way, was already commanding Nikolic. But he wanted to bring him under absolute authority or control. So Nikolic wasn't some paramilitary, to use the term.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But he was a member of the security organ. He was chief of the security organ.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was. He was the assistant commander of Pandurevic for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact his mail could go out without -- and his reports could go out without his commander reviewing his reports; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, yes, they could, but then, as I said a moment ago, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic put a stop to that, ordered that that practice be stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then was that before or after the Mladic instruction, where he set out, in detail, how he wished the commanders to be operating with the security organs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know whether conditionally speaking that conflict had any influence on the issuance of this instruction. But before we in the brigade received a similar paper of this kind, we didn't receive this order or instruction from the Main Staff, but I think that it was a similar instruction from the Drina Corps command, in actual fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in your statement that you gave back on 4 June 2003, page 87, lines 27 to 29, you say, in response to a question from Peter McCloskey: "Security officers sent the reports that even commander didn't have an access to them." Do you recall making that -- stating that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I didn't say that the security officer sent reports. What I said was that the -- not that the intelligence officer, but that the security officer did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I said intelligence, I apologise. It says here: "Security officers sent their reports that even commander didn't have an access to them." Page 87, lines 28 to 29. Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall stating that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, going on into the following page, page 88, lines 1 through 3, you say: "As the report from the security organs are the reports that he sent to the security officer in the corps. It went exclusively along their chain, and they didn't have to take it to the brigade commander to take a look." Do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did this situation ever resolve itself between Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic and Lieutenant Nikolic? Did they ever resolve their differences, come to some kind of understanding?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After a similar instruction arrived of the type I described a moment ago, Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic had to withdraw his order, the order he had given previously to the chief of the encryption office, and Drago Nikolic could do what I just said there, that is, to send out those reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So a lieutenant could send the reports that his commander, a lieutenant colonel, could not see; he could send them directly to his chain within the security organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if I might be allowed to say the following: The fact that he was second lieutenant doesn't matter. His rights didn't emanate from him being a second lieutenant and Pandurevic being lieutenant colonel, but because Drago Nikolic was chief of security. That's where his rights emanated from regardless of rank. Rank was irrelevant in this instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're right, and in fact this lieutenant could even arrest his own commander, who was a lieutenant colonel; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you an affirmative answer to that. Probably the decision should be taken at least by the corps commander. I'm not quite sure that Nikolic could make the decision to arrest Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic on his own. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic arrest Nikolic? Did he have that authority?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you indicate also in your statement - and I'm reading from page 90 - you were asked a question by Peter McCloskey, and you say -- this is with respect to vehicles, because earlier you indicate that they had their own vehicles, and you say: "Yes, but that vehicle was part of the headquarters's command and would be allocated according to the plan and the need, and the Superior Command would give it to them - when I say them, I'm referring to the security officer - put on their disposal the vehicle because they considered that their work was -- that their line of work required independence." Now, what do you mean that they considered that their line of work required independence? What are we talking about, this independence? Could you help us out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, it's like this: The essence of what I was saying and what you just quoted is that the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade had at its disposal its own vehicle, not a civilian vehicle but an army vehicle. And it was considered that this vehicle of the security organ was -- the security organ's as opposed to other vehicles in the staff command used by the command headquarters. So that vehicle was used pursuant to a decision made by Drago Nikolic. And when I said the Superior Command, when I said "them," I meant the security sector of the Drina Corps command, for them, in this way, to ensure the independence of the work of the security organs in the command of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And also, just to nail one point down. I believe you state on page 90, lines 1 to 2, that no one could open the mail of the security officer. Do you still -- do you recall making that statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that, Mr. Karnavas, except the person it was addressed to, of course. So Nikolic could open his own mail.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, of course. But Pandurevic, his commander, could not open the mail that was directed to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If, on the envelope, Mr. Karnavas, it said: "to Lieutenant Colonel Drago Nikolic in person," then mail of that kind had to go to Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And his commander could not open it up, take a little peek, see what's in it, and give it to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he could not. You're quite right on that score.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just as, conversely, when Nikolic was sending his stuff, his reports, his mail, to his -- to the security organ of the corps, the Main Staff, again, Pandurevic did not have the opportunity to look at it, see what's inside, before it went off, by courier or whatever means it went, up the chain of command to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, as we've already said, Nikolic was duty-bound in the extent to which he considered the information that was being sent out, or to the extent to which Colonel Popovic had ordered this, that he should inform Colonel Pandurevic thereof, then he should have done that, and probably he did do that. And he sent out the report, as you yourself said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to the military police, as I understand it, there were times when the security organ could use the military police for various tasks. It's a general statement. We'll get to the specific.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course, you would agree with me, would you not, that the military police was an asset, a resource, that belonged to and controlled by the commander of the brigade? Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if the rules were to be applied as they were meant to be and as they were written, then the head of the security organ, the chief of the security organ, could not, or at least should not, use the military police for whatever reason without getting prior clearance from the commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right. Commanding in the army is based on the singleness of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Explain that to us. I'm glad you mentioned that. Explain that to us so we can all understand what exactly that concept means. Seriously.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in layman's terms, one man commands. There is one man who is in command, according to the rules, as you've just said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And why is that important in an institution such as the military? Why not have two commanders at the same time, as it would appear that the Drina Corps had on the night of the 13th, at least?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- Little commentary. Completely unnecessary, not true, and gratuitous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the problem of this question is too common, you know. It's common knowledge. We don't have to prove that in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If you have a specific question, just ask this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, were there occasions when your security officer, the head of the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade, would task the military police without getting prior clearance from the commander or the deputy commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if I remember correctly, there were some minor things, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you say "minor," help us out here. What does that mean? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, if they needed to send a patrol to take somebody into custody or to control the traffic, for example, or something similar, from similar domains, that's the best I can come up with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. What about if they were engaged in what is referred to as counter-intelligence? Have you ever heard of that term, counter-intelligence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that was a function that was carried out by the security organ, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, when they carried out counter-intelligence tasks, those would be among the areas which the security organ within a brigade did not have to inform the commander and could just communicate directly through the -- through a separate chain of command to the security organ of the corps, and if necessary, the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's compound. It assumes facts not in evidence. If there's a separate chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He's going to elucidate for us. He's going to give us the answer, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If he knows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you could ask a very simple question, to the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would counter-intelligence information, or tasks, be included in some of that mail that the security organ was sending, sealed, which was not available for the commander's review before it went to the corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably yes, to a great measure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were they required, if the security organ, the chief of the security of the brigade was tasked by the security organ of the Drina Corps with a counter-intelligence mission, if I can call it that, were they required to go to the commander and say -- and tell them exactly what mission they had been given by the corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. This is a hypothetical, which is fine, but it needs to be based on facts in the -- that are relevant to this case. If he wants to use prisoners or some other fact that's relevant to this case, I haven't found any counter-intelligence yet that is relevant to this case. If there is some counter-intelligence fact that is, then that's appropriate for such a hypothetical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Under the rules, under the rules, was a security organ required to give -- to disclose their counter-intelligence missions given to them by the security organ from above to their commanders?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, as I've already stated, in the extent to which this was deemed necessary by Lieutenant Colonel Drago Nikolic or Popovic, that the commander should be informed. So then if this was considered to be a vital piece of intelligence for the unit, then they would; otherwise they would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You seem to be indicating that the discretion lay with the chief of the security organ. He would make that decision, whether his commander would know or not know. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, under the rules, if the security organ, the chief of the security organ of the brigade, was instructed by the security organ of the corps not to disclose any information to the commander, could the commander compel his chief of security to disclose it nonetheless? Could he force him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This seems to me to be an impossible situation. If the security officer said nothing, then how could the commander know that anything was there to be disclosed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Precisely. Precisely. Now, I'm going to read a portion from a statement taken by the Prosecution of Mirko Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, are we still on the same subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're on the same subject with respect to the use of the military police. We will find out that Mirko Jankovic, in his statement, informed the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go back slightly to another issue, and if we could go into private session to discuss it, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'd like to know what the issue is, Your Honour, because -- if he could give me a hint, at least I would know what issue he's referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'd like -- it's another issue that it's important that we discuss, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you asking or are you telling me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm just saying to the court deputy that we are going to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I thought the question was directed to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- Open session. And we'll resume at 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Thank you. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.36 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before we turn our attention to a statement that was given by a Mr. Jankovic, I would like to turn to a remark that you made during your testimony back on October 2nd, the second day that you testified. And this is with respect to the military police and the use of resources. And for everyone's -- for the record, I'm referring to page -- I'm afraid I'm using the unofficial version, and it's page 29. And I'm going to read to you your testimony. You were asked -- and this is starting with lines 10 through 17 -- through 15 or 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he have any authority to tell you and actually take these units? This is in reference to Mr. Nikolic, and vis-a-vis the military police.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked that of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, but militarily, did he have the authority to take those units without asking you? And your answer was:

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not. Do you recall giving that answer, that is, that Drago Nikolic did not have the authority to take the military police units and use them without prior approval? Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.
