utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to point you at your -- at what you indicated when you gave a statement back on June 4, 2003. And I'm referring to page 94, lines 27 to 33. And I'll read it back. Actually, I'm going to read from line 15 for context. Peter McCloskey is asking the questions and you're providing the answers:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And we have gone from one division to another. Let me try to work my way back. While you were deputy commander or standing in for the commander, or acting commander during this 1995 time period, you had experience dealing with Drago Nikolic from the security. Was he up to anything significant that you didn't know about it?" And your answer was:

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was up to something that I didn't know. How could I -- how could I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Or did you have any suspicions that he was using time you didn't know what he was doing? And then it's unintelligible.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's part of their job and I didn't have any suspicious. That's what they were doing at the time. That's what they -- that's what they are still doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If he was to use your troops, your materiel, would you know about it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would know if there was something significant, for example, large -- And then it's unintelligible. Do you recall being asked that question and giving -- being asked these questions and giving these answers? And I'm particularly interested in the last one, where you say: "I would know if there was something significant." Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I do recall those questions posed to me by Mr. McCloskey, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, from your statement that you gave to Mr. McCloskey, the one that I just read, it would appear, does it not, that you are implying that if the security officer used several men, or even a squad of men, you would not necessarily know or be expected to know about it? Could you be implying that, or can we make any inference?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are several questions included there, as far as I understand. However, before the break, I gave a rough reply, at least, to this question. Like I said then, something insignificant - maybe that's not a very good expression - but if there was to be a control of a moving vehicle, if he wanted to bring someone in, or something like that, that's what I was talking about a moment ago. Then Drago Nikolic himself, or another security officer, probably wouldn't have been after that, because that was part of their regular duties. This is no serious engagement for any of the units. So that's my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One second, Your Honour. I'm tangled up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, now let's turn our attention to a statement that was given by a Mr. Jankovic. And so if I could show you what has been marked for identification purposes as -- it hasn't -- it has not been marked, I'm told. So this might be, I believe, 52. Mr. Registrar, if you could assist here?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if I can assist here. It should be D54.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: 53 maybe?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D53. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if I could turn your attention -- oh, well, if we can all turn our attention to pages 53 and 54, starting with 53. It would be line 24 and all the way, I believe, to line 4. Or we can go all the way to line 10, just to make sure that it's not taken out of context. And let me read this to you. This is a -- as we indicated, Mr. -- The gentleman was being questioned by the Prosecution. He was the chief of the Bratunac military police at the time. And he's asked a question by the Prosecution investigator: "Who gave you the instructions to escort these people from this elementary school out of Bratunac?" That's page 53, line 24, 25. Answer on page 54:

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Not from the elementary school in Bratunac, but from the mechanical, the engineering school for Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who gave you the instructions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mladic personally ordered Popovic and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And before undertaking this task, did you tell your superior commander where you were going and what you were going to be doing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you informed Nikolic. Nikolic being Momir Nikolic of the Bratunac Brigade, chief of security.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was he in agreement with this decision? Answer, and this is line 11:

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This guy is superior to him. He was a higher rank in the corps, so Nikolic is subordinated to him. Before I ask my next question, I would also direct our attention to what he says on page 62 of the same interview, and I'm reading from lines 21 to 24. Well, let me go through line 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Popovic tell you what was the reason for these people to be handed over to these other soldiers??

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what this order was. That's what Mladic said, and that's also what Popovic said, that these people need to be transferred to Muslim-held territory and that from there, from that place, it's not far to the line of separation, it's not that far, quite close, and that from there, they would be taken in groups and handed over. Now, it would appear, from what Mr. Jankovic is saying, the chief of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, that he is being given a direct order by Mladic himself, General Mladic, who is the head of the VRS forces at the time. And also, at the same time, Mladic was directing Popovic, who is from the Drina Corps, the security organ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of what you just read back to me, I don't know. I was not in Bratunac myself. If I understood correctly what you just read back to me, well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, I'm not implying that you were there. I just want to make sure that you understand at least the context of what I've read. It would appear, from what I read -- I'm not saying whether it's true or whether it's false or whether you were there. No need to try to read into the question. All I'm saying is based on what I read, would it not appear that what Jankovic, the chief of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, is telling the OTP, that Mladic himself gave him a direct order? Would that -- can we conclude that that's what it appears Mr. Jankovic is saying?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the way you've read it, yes. But I'm not familiar with the position of chief of the military police. There was no chief in Zvornik, as such. There was the commander of the military police and the head was actually the chief of the security unit. But maybe there's been a misinterpretation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's just say commander. But it has nothing to do with Zvornik. There's no need to read into the question. I just want to establish the basis that your understanding of what I read, it seems that this individual, Jankovic, whatever his position may have been in the Bratunac Brigade - and we do know that he was the commander of the military police - was being ordered directly by Mladic. That's -- so can we agree that that's what it would appear from what is in his statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you've just read back, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's assume that that is correct, that Mr. Jankovic was ordered by General Mladic himself, personally, and at the same time, he's being ordered by -- he's ordering Popovic; Mladic is ordering Popovic. Is that consistent with the rules as you know them? In other words, did Mladic have the authority to give a direct order to the commander of the military police of a brigade, without having to go down the chain of command, ask the commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe is that if you stick to the rules rigorously, this is not exactly in compliance with the rules. But in view of the situation that was in place, I can't rule out the possibility that Mladic could have ordered anyone anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, is it possible -- assuming that this situation occurred the way Mr. Jankovic is describing it, how is it possible for the commander of the brigade to know what Mladic is up to with his men?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. This is so speculative that -- and it's really not up to this witness. I think this is the Court's decision, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. Karnavas. I know that you have a point here, but I wonder whether this witness is a right witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, I was trying to establish the background through his earlier statements, but I'll go about it in another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you -- let's assume that Mladic wanted to use these two individuals, Popovic of the corps, and Jankovic of the brigade. Under the rules, as you know them, what would have been the correct procedure? What should Mladic have done under these circumstances if he needed to use these resources, which obviously belong to units subordinate to him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, General Mladic would have needed to order the corps commander, and then the corps commander would have issued an order to the brigade commander. So first the corps commander to get the chief of security, Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, involved. And the commander of the Bratunac Brigade, Colonel Blagojevic, would have been ordered to get Petrovic involved in this. However, everything being as you've just read out, the duties of those two men were to report to their immediate superiors as soon as possible, on receiving orders, the orders received by Lieutenant Colonel Popovic, his duty would have been, as soon as possible, to report to General Zivanovic or General Krstic, or whoever was his immediate commander. And the other person you referred to would also have been duty-bound to report to his commander. This is a rule included in the book of rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would that reporting have to occur before they execute the task that Mladic issued, or ordered them to do, or after? In other words, could they say to the general: Excuse me, Mr. General Mladic, but I got a report. And then assuming that I get the authorisation, I'll comply with your order.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the only thing I can offer is my own interpretation, based on the assumption that you have provided. If I remember correctly, the rules of service clearly state as soon as possible, as soon as reporting is possible. At the same time, on the basis of what I myself heard and read about the procedures applied by General Mladic and his actions, I'm rather inclined to say they would have been in no position to say this loud and clear in front of him: "Sir, General, please allow me to first report to my commander." But bear in mind, please, this is only my interpretation of the situation you have given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And I take it your interpretation is based on your experience and, let's say, knowledge of General Mladic, his general personality?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, in view of my own position and duty, for most of the duration of the war I was chief of staff, and I was not very often in touch with General Mladic, only a very few times. This is only gleaned from the general atmosphere surrounding the whole situation. I may have met him personally several times, only very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you're telling us you cannot give us an opinion on that. I'll move on. Since Mladic gave this order to Commander Jankovic of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade, at that moment, is Mr. Jankovic under Mladic's authority? Who is commanding him at that moment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Establishment-wise, it would have been his own commander, but this order was given to him by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could run that by me again. I'm a little tired.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, Petrovic, I think you said the name was Petrovic,.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Jankovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jankovic, yes, his commander continued to be his commander establishment-wise, the commander of the Bratunac Brigade. And the specific order for a specific activity was obviously given to him by General Mladic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So is he under the command of General Mladic at this point in time, while he's executing this particular order that was directly ordered by General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, as he was carrying out the order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if I could go to a segment of your statement with respect to your own police platoon. As I understand your testimony here and in a statement that you gave earlier, at some point, I believe it might have been the 12th, but I might be off a little bit on the dates. 11th or 12th. A military -- a police platoon, a military police platoon from the Zvornik Brigade, went to Konjevic Polje, am I correct, to assist in the trafficking or the traffic, controlling of the road?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only partially true. It wasn't a platoon. It was just a traffic squad, or half a squad maybe. Let's say a squad. They went to Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And how many folks are in a squad? How many?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd expect about eight.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So about eight of your men, your men, were over there in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, one squad, or maybe half a squad, they went in a car, maybe five or six of them, as many as could fit in a car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to read a portion of your statement, and maybe you can help us out here a little bit. I'm reading from page 119, lines 20, from Mr. Obrenovic's statement taken on 4 June 2003. He's being questioned by Peter McCloskey:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did they report back to you or to Drago Nikolic during these days, or anyone in the command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they were reporting to anyone to the command. I think that they were subordinated to someone up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably someone in the corps. Do you recall being asked those questions and giving those answers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I don't want to complicate matters, but are you not in fact asserting that, at least with respect to these events here, that the corps was running the show and taking command and control of subordinate units of lower echelon units, such as the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I explained precisely what it was in the specific case. We received a written order, which was provided to my team by the Prosecutor in a CD. A squad or half a squad was to go to Konjevic Polje to control traffic. And I also said that upon their return - I don't know when they returned, I had lost track of that - but when the squad returned, they probably informed Jasikovac, or perhaps even Drago Nikolic, but probably they informed Jasikovac as to where they had gone to and what they had done there. And back in Konjevic Polje, as I said, they were subordinated to whoever issued their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, but these are your men. You sent them off. Aren't you told at some point who are they supposed to report to and who is going to be issuing them the tasks, into which unit they're going to be subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was stated in the same order to the person they were being sent to in Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And was that the corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was this -- this area that they were controlling, was that part of the Zvornik Brigade zone of operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karnavas. If I remember rightly, Konjevic Polje was in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably. The Zvornik area ended at the River Drinjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The zone of operation. We're not talking about responsibility now. The zone of operation, as it is specified under the rules. Okay. Now, I want to -- but just to -- before I move on: It would appear that at this point, for this particular task, your troops, your military police, were working for the corps. They're subordinated to the corps.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And can we draw some conclusion that since they were subordinated to the corps, at least for that task, whatever task they were engaged in, the corps was involved, was in control, or command and control of the subordinates that were used in those tasks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, one can draw such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go to another section of your statement, and it's page 110, lines 10 to 26. I don't know if you have your version in B/C/S, but I can read it. It's not a big section. But maybe you can --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I can -- well, it's a short section, and I'll go slowly, and it's not a terribly complex issue, or at least I think it's not. Peter McCloskey again is asking you questions, all right:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The MUP were under the command of the army at this time; is that right? That was the question. Now, MUP are the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here's your answer, and I'm reading from 110 again. That was line 10 that I just read. Line 12: "On the 19th, I don't think that it was (unintelligible) we were conducting the sweeps separately. After the corridor was closed, each group was conducting its sweeps separately. Already on the 18th, and further (unintelligible) on the 22nd there was a joint operation between the asphalt road and the gravel road in which combined units participated." Question by Peter McCloskey: "It is hard for me to imagine the MUP working in the same woods that you are working in without being under the control of the army. That would be very dangerous for both of you." Answer: "You are correct, but it was separate." Do you recall being asked those questions and giving these answers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this question was put to me by Mr. McCloskey and I replied as you read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So at least with respect to that particular task that you were describing or being -- or discussing with Mr. McCloskey, you are asserting, quite directly, if I might say, that the command and control of the MUP was separate from the army, the VRS. With respect to that limited searching in the woods. I'm not talking about some other area, but just this one right here.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, if you will allow me. Mr. McCloskey asked me about the sweep of the terrain after the closing of the corridor in the area of Krizevici, as far as Snagovo, and we commented on an intercept that was connected to this, I think. This is what you've just read out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And I guess the point that I'm trying to make is: When Mr. McCloskey obviously is very interested to know with respect to that operation whether MUP was subordinate, had been subordinated to you, to the army. I mean, that's the gist of his -- that's what he's trying to get at. And as I understand your answer, you're saying: No. We're working together, but they're not under the VRS, under your command. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact of the matter is as follows: On the 15th, at the meeting in the brigade command, part of the MUP units were put under the command of Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic, on the basis of an agreement between him and Borovcanin, and it was Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic who commanded those forces, and that's what I said. After the corridor was closed, it was probably Lieutenant Colonel Pandurevic and Borovcanin who came to an agreement and formed a staff for combing the terrain, and it was agreed that the Army of Republika Srpska, or the units deployed north of the Zvornik-Crni Vrh road should sweep Krizevici and Baljkovica to the right of the road in order to avoid confusion and the MUP units who were there were to comb the terrain to the left, or rather to the south of the asphalt road I've just mentioned, in the direction of Snagovo, and deeper, where they were moving. And the asphalt road was the border, and this was taken by our battalion, and the unit that arrived from Bratunac. They were on that road. And that's what the situation was. And that's why I said that those who were combing the southern part were under the command of the MUP in Zvornik. So the task was actually well regulated, and it was the task that actually showed whether the MUP was under the control or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I guess what I'm trying to get a handle on this: There's one particular task. It seems that you have a civilian unit, MUP; you have a military unit, yours; and you're working on the same tasks, but one is not subordinate or not in command of the other. Do I have it correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is a misstatement of the facts, of the evidence. The MUP is not a civilian unit, as I think has been established. There are civilian police officers MUP, there are Borovcanin's MUP. I mean, that's just not --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would love to debate this point, but this is not the time. But that is -- that is incorrect. They're under the civilian authorities. Now, we're going to talk about subordination and re-subordination, but it is civilian. It's not military. I can ask the gentleman the question. I think he would help me out. In fact as I believe he already indicated that MUP was civilian, if we go back in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well Mr. McCloskey, there's no time for you to argue with the Prosecution about this issue. I think if you have some doubts, or somebody has some doubts, that you have the obligation to clear it up by asking questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, was the MUP a military unit? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You're sure about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, a military unit, I don't know whether that's the proper term, but MUP means Ministry of the Interior, which is a very broad concept.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And was the Ministry of the Interior part of the civilian authorities or part of the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's part of the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And so you have the MUP, which is part of -- which is part of the civilian authorities, working in conjunction with the Zvornik Brigade, which is a military unit, on a particular task where one is not subordinate to the other, am I correct, with respect to this very narrow issue that we're discussing here today?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to tell you again that this was solved on a case-by-case basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And on this particular case, because I'm not talking about some other case; I'm talking about the case that I read, the one that Mr. McCloskey asked you about and the one to which you answered. On this particular case, is it not a fact that MUP, with the Zvornik Brigade, were working side by side and not one underneath the other? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this particular case, combing the terrain we have just mentioned, the MUP was not subordinated to the Zvornik Brigade. It operated in a separate zone, and I explained very precisely in geographic terms where they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we got the point. All right. Now, I have -- I thought maybe you could help me out with one particular term that's in Colonel Blagojevic's order. So if I could point your direction to D17/1 for identification purposes, or it might be in already as an exhibit. And if you could look at 5.5. Just look at it, glance at it, and tell me if you've ever seen or if you understand what do these letters L/RTT, what does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, I have here command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade order by the commander, number -- order for active combat actions number 1. And 5.5 is part of the commander's decision. It says reconnaissance platoon of the brigade, with LR. This means separation line. And then it says which one. So the platoon goes in a column, and then, at this line of deployment, LR --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects herself. So, it's not the separation line. It's the line of deployment.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is where they go from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, could that also mean a reconnaissance platoon of a brigade, one which had a rocket launcher? Could that -- could we -- could this have a -- that kind of meaning as well? It's not a trick question. I'm just asking you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could mean laser rocket, for all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if we read the whole sentence, reconnaissance platoon with a rocket launcher, trigonometre 707, then it doesn't make sense. If, however, we read it as follows: Reconnaissance platoon from the deployment line, trig point 707, radonjic [phoen] that means left, attacks en route, well, that's how I would read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it if you were to look at --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it could mean -- it could mean launcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, what was your relationship with the commander of the Bratunac Brigade during that period of time, July -- or leading up to July 1995, you know, while you were the chief of staff and Colonel Blagojevic was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade? What -- did you have some kind of a relationship?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, in that period, I hadn't seen Colonel Blagojevic for a long time. As I said, in the springtime I was wounded, I was on sick leave, then I got back, and there was a lot of action around Srebrenica and he probably went out into the field. And we only met up again in November 1995. As I told Mr. McCloskey in my response to his question, I was acquainted with Colonel Blagojevic. He worked in the corps command, and we would meet. And I think our relations were correct, but we didn't know each other especially well. It was a superficial acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it during this critical period that we've been discussing, either you didn't have a need to or the opportunity to come into contact with Colonel Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You are right. I didn't contact him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm pleased to announce that, as promised, I am through with my cross-examination, a little bit longer than I wanted to, but ... Oh, I should note for the record that the June 4, 2003 statement is D52/1 for identification purposes. I apologise for not making the record clear. So I have no further questions at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Any cross-examination, Ms. Sinatra?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was wondering if I might have a moment to organise my thoughts, or if we could continue at 2.00 tomorrow. I promise I'll be finished in tomorrow and Thursday, during those days. So Friday we have redirect and questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we still have 40 minutes. I think it's too long to have a break. Why not you start right now and see how far you could go? I believe that before the cross-examination you have some questions about the background, the foundation issues. Why not use this moment? Because 40 minutes is a long period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I really don't have background information, and I worked with the audiovisual department to have the camera set up for the model I was going to use. And my first line of questioning was building the foundation for the model. But Mr. Karnavas assured me he would use all the time today. It would take us a few minutes to get set up, if the Trial Chamber would allow me to ask AV to come in and try to get all this set up again. We marked it here so that we would have it first thing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I wonder whether if we could have it set up in 10 minutes, so at least we have 30 minutes this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe we probably could. I'm assuming that the AV department is willing to come set it up for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a short break until 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. --- Break taken at 3.51 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sinatra, you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, for being so tolerant with the theatrics that we have in the courtroom. I would like to spend the next few moments laying the foundation for the use of this model. I would also like to ask the Court to consider the use of this model under the Rules of Evidence, 89, and also Rule 98, to allow the Trial Chamber to allow for additional evidence in the courtroom. I'd like to start with introducing to the Court, which I don't have copies - I promise to provide tomorrow - which are the original -- this would be D -- marked for identification purposes only as D7. These are the original architectural drawings and mechanical drawings from the Standard factory, which is a shoe factory, in the municipality of Zvornik, which was used for headquarters, Zvornik Brigade headquarters, and I will elicit this testimony from Mr. Obrenovic in a moment but I wanted to get the documents out of the way first if the Court would tolerate this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Before you start, could I ask you a question? Are you going to use these kind of mechanisms tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am. And I probably will use it all through the cross, and I encourage the Prosecution and other Defence counsel to utilise the model in the courtroom throughout the rest of the trial, if they choose to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this moment, I'd just advise you that tomorrow morning this courtroom may be used for another purpose. So I hope that before we start tomorrow afternoon, everything will be in place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have it taped and marked and they can move the camera on short notice, and the model exhibit is on rollers, so it will roll to the side of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I also would like to -- for the Court's permission, which Mr. McCloskey and opposing counsel except for Mr. Karnavas have seen, is the curriculum vitae of the model builder, Mr. Postma. I didn't think it was possible to call him as a witness. He has a letter of the dimensions and proportions of the model built in here. The photographs that he used were 1:200 scale and the model itself is built on a 1:100 scale. So if I might introduce now what's been marked for identification as D8, which is the curriculum vitae and information of the model builder. Thank you. We will provide copies of all that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Sinatra.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Dobar dan. I have given you a chance earlier to have a look at this model and I gave you the plans of the model that you were able to take at your break and inspect. Does this model accurately reflect the way the Zvornik Brigade headquarters looked in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, excuse me. Today, during one of the breaks, I spent about ten minutes looking at this model, and as I said then, I'm no architect myself, I'm no engineer, but roughly speaking, this looks like it, at least from the outside. This looks very much like the building where the command was based in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Just for further identification purposes and for the purposes of the Trial Chamber, Mr. Usher, I would like now to go through just a series of photographs and use the ELMO, which are photographs of the -- well, I'll let the witness identify these. We'll go through these. This will be D25 and then it will be .1, .2, .3, as we go through. And this is the exterior. This would be marked D25.1. Mr. Obrenovic, can you identify this picture? I know it's kind of difficult.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, it appears that in this photograph marked as number 19, we can see the side of the building of the brigade headquarters, one of its sides. This is from -- looking from the River Drina, and you can see the south side of the building, the side facing south. At least, that's how it appears to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Do you still have your pointer on the witness stand?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Just for -- I don't want you to switch back, but for the Trial Chamber's information, could you point on the model where you think this photograph is, which corner. Which direction is facing toward the Judges right now, of the model?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, I think this part here, this section. I can't be sure, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And may the record reflect that the witness has identified as facing the model to the right rear of the model. And I'm sorry, Mr. Usher. May we have the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, can you identify what this photograph is, represents?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, I believe that what I can see here is one of the warehouses, or rather, hangars. The photo was taken from the rear, near the Drina River, this photograph marked as 25. That's what I think it is. So this is not the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: No, it's not. It's one of the buildings that's not included in the model; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Can we have the next photograph, please. Actually, if you go on to the next one. I think that's a duplicate. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And Mr. Obrenovic, can you identify this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, I'm looking at this photograph marked as 23. I believe this is again the warehouse, what I see in front. At the back you have the heating pipes, the steam heating. This thing at the front, this may have been the workshop.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And could we have the next photograph, please. I'm sorry. I think that's a duplicate. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Now, what does this photograph represent? If you can't identify it, then that's all right, but I believe that it is taken from the Drina side of the compound.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In photograph 20, I believe we are again looking at one section of the brigade headquarters, the building, that is, looking from the Drina River. I believe this is very much like the one we saw a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Could we have the next photograph, please. And I've lost count, Mr. Registrar. It's 25. --?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be 25.4/3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Obrenovic, can you identify this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, photograph number 26, the central portion of the photograph, shows a road inside the barracks, part of the parking lot, and to the left, the way I'm looking, I see a section of one of the warehouses inside the factory compound. In the background, you can see a bus, I think. And then some houses in the Karakaj village, and then the hills behind.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And, Mr. Obrenovic, the headquarters for the Zvornik Brigade is located in a village called Karakaj; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, the Zvornik Brigade command was located in a building inside the compound of the building you've mentioned. We called it Standard, and the whole thing was in the village of Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And Standard stands for the Standard Shoe Manufacturing Company, which was the manufacturing company in the building prior to you taking it over as military headquarters; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but your question has two parts, in a manner of speaking, and I have to reply with two answers. The first part of the question: It is true that there used to be a shoe manufacturer in these premises called Standard. That was earlier. As for the second part of your question, I did not set up the barracks or the command myself. When I arrived at the scene, it was already there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: The headquarters is referred to many times as Standard, and that stands for the manufacturing company that was once present in the building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, as far as I know, the command was called -- well, for a while, at least, it was called the command of the 1st Light Infantry Zvornik Brigade. After that it was called the command of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade, and then some other people may have used the word "Standard" to refer to the building. But establishment-wise it was always the headquarters of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: I heard you refer to the building as Standard, and that's why I was trying to clarify it for the Trial Chamber. And Standard is a term used throughout a lot of statements and many information reports. So just for clarification for the Trial Chamber Standard is another term used for the Zvornik Brigade headquarters because a manufacturing company used to be there that was called Standard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, I don't think that's quite right. If we choose to generalise like this, it would be more accurate to say that the term "Standard" referred to the barracks, or the compound. So whatever was inside the compound, people would say: In Standard. But the word "Standard" cannot refer to the command because that was not the only thing that was there. There were four or five other units too.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Can we go on to the next photograph, please. This would be marked D25.6/3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic, can you identify the main headquarters building from this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, I'm looking at photograph number 28, and this appears to have been taken from the north, facing south. There's a road with these cars. And in the left corner I can see one section of the warehouse. And you can see a building further down where the headquarters of the brigade was, its northern and western face, if I've got my bearing correctly. From the north, facing south.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: So if you were facing the back of the building, this would be the right-hand side of the back of the building, or the side?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, if I've got my bearings right, I think this is the main facade of the building, this is the entrance, and this is the northern face of the building. If you face it directly, what I said before, this is the left hand part of the building, if I'm facing the building, and this should be the entrance to the building. Yes, that should be it, that's if I've got my bearings right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Obrenovic, this is a photograph from the front of the building?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the gate on your right, under the number 4, would be the gate that goes out onto the main road between Zvornik and Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right I can see a section of another building, which may be the building where the reporting officer used to be, or reception.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: But the road that goes from Zvornik to Bijeljina is behind the gate to the right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, I think this road runs parallel to this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. That's the way I perceived it also. Now, from these photographs, so that we don't have to go through a whole stack, is it your opinion that the exterior of the model accurately represents the Zvornik Brigade headquarters in 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, this is a rough rendering, yes. The floors are correct. Truth to tell, I can't remember the exact number of windows that were there. But roughly what I can see here, that might be it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: If I might ask the usher's assistance to turn the model around, and we could get on the video monitor the front of the building. If we could have the audiovisual operator. Thank you. Your Honour, I hope you don't mind if we use the AV operator to focus in the camera instead of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. And before we leave the photos, Ms. Sinatra, would you please tell me the author of these photos, I mean who took these pictures.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: The photos were taken by our investigator in Zvornik, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And when?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Well, a month ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Thank you. On the video monitor, could we get a front on the building now? Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Now, can you see the front of the building on your monitor, Mr. Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, this is a bird's eye view of the model, the bird-eye view, I'd say, the front of the building with and the entrance and what should be the roof, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes. And Mr. Obrenovic, if I could have the usher's assistance to turn the model around, and could we zoom in on the perspective that's built into the model, which is on the back. No, no, no. Turn it around. Mr. Obrenovic, I had you look at this perspective, which is just built in as part of the back side of the model, today, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I looked at it briefly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: What does this small perspective of the Standard compound represent to you? Can you describe the area and the compound for the Trial Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, this is probably a model built on a certain scale, the factory we're talking about, the Standard shoe manufacturer, where some of the units in the command of the Zvornik Brigade were stationed in July 1995. Roughly speaking, I think it corresponds to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Would you please use your photo -- I mean your pointer, and point to the building that is represented here as the Zvornik Brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this section of the model is the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And the road out front is the main highway between Zvornik and Bijeljina, going north along the Drina River; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's one section of the road, yes. But not running parallel to the River Drina, but rather outside the barracks. It was the barracks that stood between the road and the river.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: And could you please point to the Drina River on the model.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, it's difficult for me to say what this green colour here stands for, if that's the river. But it was on this side from these last buildings over here, there was an asphalt road, and after that there was a belt, maybe between 50 and 70 metres wide, an area, and then the river. So the river is here, to the back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: The extension from the back of the model of the Zvornik Brigade, can you point that area out on the perspective, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Yes. And does that little extension coming off the back of the building, that goes on to the other buildings which were considered the barracks, the larger buildings that were part of the Standard compound?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN OBRENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ms. Sinatra, if memory serves me, this is a hall, a corridor, between the brigade command, the headquarters, and the remaining buildings. There was a corridor. Once you've passed the corridor, there was the building where the kitchen was, and the medical unit, the clinic, and then through that building you could reach the hangars. Some of the doors were kept closed, because there were many different things being kept, obviously, in the hangars.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: If we could -- if I could ask the usher's assistance to turn the model around to the front again. Your Honours, I'm about to start the interior of the building. Should we save that for tomorrow or should I proceed with it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think it's time for a break, so you may continue tomorrow afternoon. And I have been advised that, as I said before, this courtroom will be used for another trial. So I hope that before leaving this courtroom, everybody should take their personal belongings out of the courtroom. And we'll resume at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: The model has remained in the courtroom on the trolley over here behind the defence bar. May we leave the model covered up in the courtroom? It's safer here and it's protected here from tampering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe so. I'll entrust the court deputy to see to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SINATRA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
